9241.t: From ἀριστόβουλος (aristóboulos, “best in counsel”) from ἄριστος (áristos, “best”) and βουλή (boulḗ, “counsel”).

9249.t: Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀏𐀹𐀊𐀆 (a-ka-wi-ja-de), Hittite 𒆳𒌷𒄴𒄭𒅀𒉿𒀀 (Aḫḫiyawā), Egyptian jqꜣwꜣšꜣ (Ekwesh). Beekes reconstructs Pre-Greek *Akayʷa.

9242.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos Proto-Hellenic *árktos Ancient Greek ἄρκτος (ắrktos) Proto-Indo-European *wer-der.

9248.t: From Old Median *R̥štivaigah, modified by folk etymology (compare ἄστυ (ắstŭ, “city”) and ἄγνυμι (ắgnūmĭ, “to break”) and compound names ending in -αγης (-agēs)).

9239.t: From Ἀργε- (Ărge-, oblique stem of Ἄργος (Ắrgos)) + -ιος (-ĭos).

9213.t: Has been derived from Proto-Indo-European *terkʷ-, with cognates including Sanskrit तर्कु (tarku), Albanian dredh and Latin torqueō.

9273.t: A reduplicative adjectival formation from ἐγείρω (egeírō, “to awaken”) + -ος (-os).

9226.t: Traditionally taken from an earlier *ἄνσθμα (*ánsthma), potentially a derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂enh₁- (“to breathe”) with an extension of unclear origin, followed by the suffix -μα (-ma) (from Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥).

9221.t: From ἅλλομαι (hắllomai, “to jump, to leap”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

9211.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sn̥Hter (whence also Proto-Germanic *sunder (“apart; separately”)), from *senH-; cognate with ἄνευ (ắneu), as well as Latin sine and Sanskrit स॒नि॒तुर् (sanitúr)).

9208.t: Verbal adjective of ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + σῴζω (sōízō, “to save”).

9287.t: From ἐκεῖ (ekeî, “yonder”) + -σε (-se, “towards”). This is the expected distal destination demonstrative reflex.

9222.t: From an earlier *ϝάλυτις (*wálutis), with original sense of "winding (object)", derived from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind”) (though the α (a) remains phonetically unexplained).

9209.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not, without”) + τάσσω (tássō, “draw up in order of battle, form, array, marshal”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix).

9232.t: From ἀμόρα (amóra) + -ιον (-ĭon), or related to ἀμόργη (ămórgē, “pressed olives; dye”), or possibly of Semitic stem relation to Biblical Hebrew עֲמֹרָה (ʿĂmōrā) from a root meaning "deep with water" (a city name transcribed in the LXX as Γόμορρα (Gómorrha)).

9200.t: From ἀ- (a-) + ῥήγνυμι (rhḗgnūmi, “to break, shatter”) + -τος (-tos, adjective suffix).

9225.t: Compound of ἅ (há) + τε (te). Compare ὅτε (hóte), τότε (tóte), πότε (póte).

9206.t: From ἀ- (ă-) + the root of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ) + -τος (-tos)

9224.t: From the same uncertain origin as ἁρπάζω (harpázō).
